title: Pneumonia, lung abscess, empyema and respiratory arrest in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the main lung condition (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/18/2026
Reason for Admission: Aspiration pneumonia

Vitals:
T: 98.4 F, HR: 78, BP: 132/84, RR: 18, SpO2: 95% on RA.

Labs:
WBC: 12.4, Hgb: 13.2, Hct: 39.5, Cr: 1.1, BUN: 18, Na: 138, K: 4.0.

Review of Systems:
Resp: Productive cough, SOB. Chest: Clear to auscultation. GI: No nausea, no diarrhea. Neuro: Alert and oriented x3.

Social History:
Lives at home with spouse. Former smoker (quit 20 years ago). No alcohol use.

Family History:
Father: Hypertension. Mother: Type 2 DM.

Hospital Course:
Pt is a 90-year-old male admitted for aspiration pneumonia after a choking episode involving food at home. Pt presented with fever, tachypnea, and productive cough. Started on IV antibiotics and supplemental oxygen as needed. Chest X-ray confirmed infiltrate. Pt tolerated oral intake but showed signs of dysphagia. Speech therapy and a swallow evaluation were performed. Pt showed improvement in clinical status and was able to tolerate thickened liquids. Antibiotics completed. Pt stable for discharge to home with outpatient follow-up.

Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Aspiration pneumonia
2. Dysphagia

Discharge Medications:
1. Amoxicillin 500mg BID x 7 days
2. Acetaminophen 650mg PRN for pain/fever
3. Thickened liquids diet per SL

Follow-up:
F/u with Primary Care Physician in 1 week. F/u with Speech Therapy in 10 days.

Electronically signed, L. Moreau, MD, 05/18/2026
explanations: Aspiration pneumonia: pneumonitis due to inhalation of food and vomit, J69.0 (HCC 282).
refs: ICD-10-CM Tabular: J15-J18, J69, J85-J86, R09

distractors.why: Aspiration pneumonia has its own code (HCC 282).
